name: Forma / Forma-i

lead: Forma and Forma-i are InMode radiofrequency devices used in clinics to tighten skin on the face and body. The idea is to warm the deeper skin so it builds fresh collagen, giving a firmer, lifted look along the jawline and cheeks.
It is non-surgical and typically delivered over several sessions by a clinician.

paras: RF energy heats the dermis, which is intended to stimulate collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid production and so reduce laxity and fine lines.
RF treatments in general have been associated with pain, dents from uneven healing, and rarely fat necrosis or scarring; newer techniques aim to reduce these.

chain: Heating prompts collagen and elastin remodeling
Skin looks firmer and the jawline and cheeks look tighter
angle.text: Clinics use facial RF to tighten loose skin around the jowls, cheeks and neck, which can give a sharper lower-face outline. Treatment is non-surgical and is usually done as a series of sessions.

lead: Forma and Forma-i are radiofrequency (RF) devices from the aesthetics company InMode that are used in clinics for non-surgical skin tightening of the face and body. Practitioners offer them as a way to firm lax skin along the jawline, cheeks and neck, giving a tighter, more defined lower face without surgery.[1]

Radiofrequency skin tightening in general works by heating the deeper layers of skin to stimulate the body to make new collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid, which is intended to soften fine lines and lift loose skin.[1] People in looksmaxxing circles file facial RF under non-invasive "hardmaxxing" procedures, alongside other clinic-based treatments aimed at jawline and skin definition.
This entry describes the category of treatment in general terms; brand-specific results and protocols are set by clinics and the manufacturer.

paras: RF devices pass radio-frequency energy through the skin to heat the dermis. The heat is intended to trigger collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid production, and a dermal temperature of roughly 67 degrees Celsius has been described as ideal for remodeling and reducing laxity.[1] Penetration depth depends on the electrode design, with monopolar, bipolar and unipolar arrangements in use.[1]

RF skin tightening is used on the jowls, abdomen, thighs and arms, and for wrinkle reduction, cellulite and body contouring.[1] In facial work the usual aim is a firmer, tighter-looking lower face and neck.

Reported effects of RF treatments in general include pain significant enough to require sedation in some patients, surface dents from uneven healing when energy is applied improperly, and, rarely, fat necrosis and atrophic scarring; newer techniques are described as addressing these problems.[1]
No studies found. Studies of radiofrequency skin tightening as a broader category, including comparisons with surgical facelifts, are summarized in general references.[1]
